rationale: A wins because it sees the live business story B threw in the bin: "Calm goes from $70-a-year subscription to a covered insurance benefit for 25 million members" is the sharpest founder-useful angle here. B is competent, but "Business/revenue mechanics — no_journalist_shape" is exactly backwards; undisclosed economics are not a reason to kill the angle, they are the angle. A also keeps the trend claim honest by saying comparables must be supplied, while B tries to make "The Wellness-to-Clinical Shift Is Arriving" carry more weight than one deal can bear.
gaps_in_A: "Wellness apps are crossing from app-store impulse buy into reimbursed health benefit" is a trend headline built on one Calm deal; A qualifies it later, but the headline still outruns the proof.
"once growth slows" imports a subscription-market slowdown frame that is not in the supplied update.
"sponsored-research skepticism journalists are writing about right now" adds a vague external peg; the facts already support scrutiny without that garnish.
gaps_in_B: "Business/revenue mechanics — no_journalist_shape" is the big miss. No revenue terms disclosed is not a blocker; it is the reporter's question.
"The Wellness-to-Clinical Shift Is Arriving" overclaims a category shift from one payer deal and one Calm-funded study.
"The Number That Moves Clinicians" invents clinician reaction. The update gives an 18% self-reported reduction, not evidence that clinicians care.
"from pharmaceutical research, food science, and now digital health" smuggles in external background claims. That may be true, but it is not in the update and needs sourcing.
